comment: Source-backed native lowering - coverage and prioritisation of the captured guest CPU. Built from the PMC guest CPU capture of 2026-10-19 (guest thread 52152 of CrashNative.exe sha256 2eabbce77a00067ba361c282c17907076a42c6ccd70800337d44c64b0674f3fa), the completed build clean-room-guest-batch-20261019-2 generated guest tree, and the repository reference data (native-port/data/native-lowering-candidates.json, native-port/data/native-lowering-inventory.json, native-port/data/plain-leaf-family.json, native-port/reference/guest-regions/linked-regions.json, native-port/reference/guest-regions/effect-exclusions.json). All "sampled_share" numbers are timer sample shares of the 42211 guest-thread timer samples; they are NOT host instruction counts, NOT host cycle counts and NOT per-function CPI. The host counters in the capture (50,012,170 retired host x86 instructions per XFB, 43,515,534 host cycles per XFB, aggregate host CPI 0.87010, 10.9939 ms scheduled guest CPU per XFB) are thread-level and are not attributable to a function by this capture. The two capture windows (44.82446 s / 3847 XFB at 85.82 XFB/s and 29.80633 s / 2684 XFB at 90.05 XFB/s) are separate scene windows and are not a controlled A/B.

capture.windows: two separate scene windows: pass 1 (cycles/instructions) 44.82446 s, 3847 XFB copies, 85.8237 XFB/s; pass 2 (branch/cache) 29.80633 s, 2684 XFB copies, 90.0480 XFB/s. They are not a controlled A/B and their event totals must not be combined.

host_counters_not_attributable_per_funct.note: thread-level hardware counters; no per-function CPI, no per-function cache attribution, and timer-sample attribution carries sampling skid.

denominators.note: all_guest_samples = every timer sample attributed to the guest thread in the first-pass common window (42211). non_external_guest_samples = the same minus the 2015 samples whose IP fell outside the module (40196). translated_guest_function_samples = the 31720 samples that the capture attributed to a translated guest function body after collapsing the host symbol aliases (func_X, func_X.cold, func_X_kernel, native_guest_primary_X, native_guest_resume_X, native_guest_continuation_X and their .cold clones). The capture's own "generated guest" group is 31792 samples; the 72-sample difference is 58 samples of native_guest_regions::Enabled() / native_guest_loop::Enabled() and 14 samples of native_block_* bounded-block wrappers, which are runtime helpers mis-grouped by the capture's prefix rule.
denominators.share_denominator_used_in_this_file: all_guest_samples (42211) unless a field says otherwise

method.static_call_site_counting: Every generated chunk under C:\Users\deki\.codex\native-port-builds\clean-room-guest-batch-20261019-2\storage\crash-generated\*.cpp (95 files) was parsed into guest function bodies. A static call site is one occurrence of the pattern `func_<addr>(ctx)` inside a guest function body, i.e. the generated form of `ctx.pc = 0x<addr>; func_<addr>(ctx);` (79206 occurrences) or the tail-call form `ctx.pc = 0x<addr>; { if(native_guest_fast::TailEnter()) ... func_<addr>(ctx); ... }` (1728 occurrences), for 80934 direct guest call sites in total. The guest function boundary table in main_output.cpp (`{0x<start>, 0x<end>, func_<start>}`) is a dispatch/interior-entry registry, not a call site, and is deliberately NOT counted. Self-calls are not counted. A function with 0 call sites is reached through the guest indirect/dispatch path.
method.alias_collapse: All host symbols that map to the same guest address are collapsed onto that address before any arithmetic. 153 alias groups were found; the largest is 803143EC with 6 symbols and 2792 samples.
method.clone_collapse: Two clone kinds are reported: (a) byte-identical machine code (same text_sha256) from native-port/data/native-lowering-inventory.json, and (b) near-clones found in this session by hashing the generated body after normalising register indices, 8-digit hex constants and label names. A body-exact hash of the generated tree found 0 exact duplicates, so all clones in the generated tree are near-clones.
method.dynamic_call_counts: Never inferred from timer samples. Where a call site sits inside a data-dependent loop the member records the loop and says the dynamic count scales with its trip count, which the capture does not measure.
method.feasibility_text: For the 337 source-backed addresses the feasibility string is taken verbatim from native-port/data/native-lowering-inventory.json (MMIO/BP stores, RAM reads and writes, psq use, MSR.FP guards, loop back edges, poll points, interior entries, translated instruction count). For the no-source addresses it is derived in this session from the generated body.

top10_operations.complete_operation: the whole descriptor-driven vertex emitter of func_803143EC: walk the vertex-format descriptor (rlwinm tests on bits 0x1b/0x14/0x13/0x1a/0x11/0x17), load each attribute from the vertex array, convert it to the packed form the GX pipeline wants, emit the packed words to the write-gather pipe at 0xCC008000, and update the object AABB, including the 26 poll points and the plane/sqrt tests at the end.
top10_operations.why: One bounded native kernel is feasible in principle: the emitter is a single function with a register-resident descriptor, no re-entry, and a guard predicate (native_gx_emitter_ready, no watch, MEM1-resident descriptor) that already exists. The kernel native_vertex_emit_803143EC is already derived and shipped, so the work is to make the hot-split primary entry dispatch into it, not to write it. It CANNOT be covered from recovered source: no source for 803143EC exists.

top10_operations.complete_operation: the whole guest driver body of func_803DB050 (65 interior entries, 25 RAM writes, 2 poll points, 2 loop back edges) including its two guest calls.
top10_operations.why: Cannot be covered as one bounded native kernel without a recovered source: the function is a re-entrant driver body with interior entries and polls, and no C/C++ source exists for it in the repository. Only a translation-derived (not source-backed) kernel could address it.

top10_operations.complete_operation: the whole GXSetFog call: read the SDA fog constants, convert the five float arguments through the psq round-trip, pack the fog register word and issue the ten BP-register stores (5 x 32-bit payload + 5 x 8-bit flag) at 0xCC008000, plus the one guest-RAM write and the two poll points.
top10_operations.why: Bounded: one function, one MMIO port, no re-entry, no data-dependent loop that depends on guest state beyond the argument conversion. It cannot be covered completely today because the function has 51 interior entries in its dispatch prologue and 1 data-dependent back edge, so the native entry has to keep the translated body reachable and only the ordinary entry can be replaced (the pattern already used by GXSetFogRangeAdj/GXSetChanCtrl).

top10_operations.complete_operation: the whole per-material draw path of func_802FDB74: take the material object, read the descriptor from vtable[0x50], emit the material's vertex groups and issue the 7 virtual dispatches, the 198 write-gather stores and the 13 poll points.
top10_operations.why: NOT coverable as one bounded kernel: the path keeps 7 virtual (vtable) dispatches and calls 802A9300/802A94C4/80281A94/803A3480/803A3074, so it is not a register-local leaf. The stage docstring (tools/vertex_emit_kernel.py) states this explicitly and leaves it out on purpose: it would need its own seeded object graph and oracle driver. No recovered source either.
